record.field: Your Bank in Odoo: Set Up Right, Reconcile Every Month

field.name: description
field.p: Set each bank account up once so most of the statement books itself, then turn every monthly statement into books that match the bank to the cent.

div.p: If you've kept books in a check register, you're used to entering a payment and then ticking it off when it clears. Odoo works the other way round: the bank's statement comes in, and you explain each line on it. That's what reconciling is.

Every line you import is booked to your bank account straight away, so Odoo's bank balance always follows the real one. What each line was (a customer paying, a purchase, a transfer, your own money) is the part you, or a rule, fill in.
When every line is explained, your profit and loss, what customers still owe you and what you owe suppliers are all true, because the bank has confirmed each one.
Until a line is explained, Odoo parks it in a holding account. Knowing the four of them makes every screen in this course easier to read:

ul.li: Bank Suspense: a bank line nobody has explained yet. It should be empty once you've reconciled.
Outstanding Receipts: a payment you recorded on an invoice (Register Payment), waiting for the bank line that brings the money in.
Outstanding Payments: the same for money you've recorded paying out.
Liquidity Transfer: money moving between two of your own accounts, waiting until both statements show it.

div.p: Reconciling a line moves it out of the holding account and onto what it really was: the invoice it paid, the bill it settled, an expense, or your own money going in or out.

div.span: Read a balance like a to-do list
div.p: Anything left in these holding accounts is something not yet matched. After a month is reconciled, Bank Suspense and Liquidity Transfer should both be zero.

In Odoo a bank account is a journal of the type Bank. Give each real account its own: checking, savings, a business credit card. Each one has its own statement and its own balance, so mixing two in one journal can never match.

In Accounting › Configuration › Accounting › Journals open your bank or click New. Name it so you can't mix it up (bank name and account type), enter the Bank Account Number, and set Bank Feeds to Import File.

Screenshota checking account set up as a bank journal. the sample business in these screenshots is Juniper Hollow Design, with a second business name, Juniper Hollow Photo, banking at Cedar Valley Credit Union. All made up.

Some banks keep deposits in savings and move money into checking whenever a card purchase posts. Give savings its own journal too: each top-up then shows on both statements, and a rule books both halves to Liquidity Transfer (see Rules for the regulars).

The easiest start is the day the account opens, at zero. If it already had money in it when you started using Odoo, book that opening balance once with a journal entry against your Capital account, dated the day before your first statement line, so Odoo's balance starts where the bank's did.
Download your statement from online banking as a CSV file: the PDF statement is for reading, the CSV is for importing. Ask for one file per account.
Each bank lays its file out a little differently, so tell Odoo once which column is which in Accounting › Configuration › Accounting › Statement Sheet Mappings:

ul.li: Timestamp Format: how dates are written, for example %m/%d/%y for 10/14/26.
Amount column: the signed amount (money out is negative). A $ sign and thousands commas are fine.
Unique transaction ID column: the bank's own ID for each line. With it, importing the same file twice skips the lines you already have.
Description Column: the short name you'll see when reconciling, and Notes Column for the bank's longer detail.

img.alt: The columns of a statement file layout

div.p: Screenshotthe columns of a credit union's CSV layout.

div.span: Leave Balance Column empty if your bank leaves gaps
div.p: Some banks fill the running balance on only some rows. Odoo would then take a wrong ending balance from the file. Without it you check the ending balance against the statement yourself, which is the real test anyway.
Then pick the layout on each bank journal as its default, and the import fills it in for you.
Lines that look the same every month don't need you. In Accounting › Configuration › Accounting › Reconciliation Models a rule says: when a line's label contains these words, book it to this account.
Screenshotrules for top-ups and the owner's own money (Automated), plus buttons for the odd ones out (Manual).

ul.li: Automated rules book matching lines as soon as they're imported.
Manual rules become buttons on the reconcile screen, for lines you want to look at first, such as cash withdrawals or bank fees.

div.p: Screenshotevery line on checking whose label contains Transfer From Share 01 is a top-up from savings, booked to Liquidity Transfer.

Copy the words from your own statement's labels: the part that's always the same, such as Transfer From Share 01 or the name on your personal account. Limit a rule to the journals it belongs to, and check its first month's results.

record.field: Your own money, and your business names

div.p: When you own the business yourself, money moves between you and it. Keep that out of your profit and loss:

ul.li: Money you put in from your personal account goes to Capital (owner contribution).
Money you take out goes to Owner Draws. If your chart has no such account, add one in Accounting › Configuration › Accounting › Chart of Accounts with the type Equity.
A cash withdrawal you can't tie to a receipt is usually a draw. Ask your tax preparer what fits your situation.

div.span: A customer paid into your personal account?
div.p: Register the payment on the invoice as usual. It then waits in Outstanding Receipts, because no business bank line will ever arrive for it. Clear it with a journal entry from Outstanding Receipts to Owner Draws (the money is yours now), and match the two in Accounting › Accounting › Reconcile. Never book it against the bank account itself: the business bank never saw that money, and its balance would stop matching.

If you trade under more than one business name, Odoo can treat each one as a branch of your company: one business and one bank, but a separate profit and loss per name. Switch to the branch in the company menu at the top right and enter its bills there. The main company's bank lines can still be matched to them.

img.alt: A vendor bill for a branch

div.p: Screenshota bill entered under the branch, Juniper Hollow Photo, and paid from the main company's checking.

ol.li: In online banking, export each account as CSV for exactly the statement's dates.
On the Accounting › Dashboard, click Import File on that account's card (on some installs it says Import (OCA)).
Your bank's layout is already chosen. Upload the file and click Import and Start to Reconcile, or Import and View to look at the statement first.

div.p: Screenshotafter importing: the rules have done most of it, and each card says how many lines still need you.
Screenshotimporting a statement file.
For purchases, enter the vendor bill with its receipt attached before you reconcile (in the right business name, if you have branches). Then each card purchase is a one-click match.

Click Reconcile N Items on the card. The statement lines are on the left. For the selected line, the right side shows its bank line, the part still waiting in Bank Suspense, your rule buttons, and the tabs.
Screenshota card purchase still in Bank Suspense. Typing the vendor's name in the Reconcile tab's search finds its bill.

ol.li: In the Reconcile tab, search for the customer or vendor and click the invoice, bill or payment the line belongs to.
Or click a rule button, such as Bank Fees, for a line with no invoice behind it.
Or use Manual operation to choose the account yourself.
When nothing is left in Bank Suspense, Reconcile lights up. Click it.

img.alt: A line matched to its bill

div.p: Screenshotthe bill has replaced Bank Suspense, so Reconcile is ready.
Click To Check and move on: the line keeps its place, and you or your bookkeeper can come back to it.
A month is done when Odoo agrees with the bank, not just when the list is empty:

ul.li: Each bank card's Balance on the dashboard equals the ending balance on that account's statement.
Bank Suspense is zero: nothing left unexplained.
Liquidity Transfer is zero: every transfer shows on both accounts.
Outstanding Receipts and Outstanding Payments hold only payments too recent to be on this statement.

div.p: Check the accounts in Accounting › Reporting with a trial balance dated the statement's last day. Then set a lock date for the month so nothing changes it by accident: see Fiscal years and lock dates in the course Getting Paid and Keeping the Books.
When the dashboard balance and the statement disagree, the difference is almost always one of these:

ul.li: Something posted straight to the bank account without a statement line, such as a journal entry. Open the bank account in Accounting › Configuration › Accounting › Chart of Accounts, look at its journal items, and find the ones with no statement line. Move each to the account it really belongs to (often Outstanding Receipts or Owner Draws).
A file imported for the wrong dates, so a line is missing or belongs to next month. Compare the dates in Odoo with the statement's.
The same transaction twice, from a file without transaction IDs. Delete the extra statement line.
A top-up booked on one account only. Liquidity Transfer then isn't zero: import the other account's statement too.

div.p: Search the journal items for the exact difference. A single amount that explains the gap is usually one entry in the wrong place.
